```{python}
#| include: false
"""
Schematic diagrams of 8 deep learning architectures, drawn with matplotlib.

Model names: "feedforward", "cnn", "rnn", "autoencoder",
             "transformer", "mamba", "gan", "gnn"
"""
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import Circle, FancyArrowPatch, FancyBboxPatch, Rectangle

# ---- shared colors (same as the earlier network diagram) -------------------
BLUE, ORANGE, GREEN = "#4C72B0", "#DD8452", "#55A868"
PURPLE, RED, GRAY, LIGHT = "#8172B3", "#C44E52", "#8C8C8C", "#D9D9D9"


# ---- small drawing helpers ---------------------------------------------------
def _setup(ax):
    """Every panel uses the same 10 x 6 canvas."""
    ax.set_xlim(0, 10)
    ax.set_ylim(0, 6)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.axis("off")


def _node(ax, x, y, color, r=0.28, text="", fs=8):
    ax.add_patch(Circle((x, y), r, facecolor=color, edgecolor="black", lw=1, zorder=3))
    if text:
        ax.text(x, y, text, ha="center", va="center", fontsize=fs, color="white", zorder=4)


def _line(ax, p, q, color=GRAY, lw=0.7, alpha=0.6):
    ax.plot([p[0], q[0]], [p[1], q[1]], color=color, lw=lw, alpha=alpha, zorder=1)


def _arrow(ax, p, q, color="black", lw=1.4, ls="-", rad=0.0):
    ax.add_patch(FancyArrowPatch(p, q, arrowstyle="-|>", mutation_scale=12, color=color,
                                 lw=lw, linestyle=ls, zorder=2,
                                 connectionstyle=f"arc3,rad={rad}"))


def _box(ax, x, y, w, h, color, text="", fs=9, tc="white"):
    ax.add_patch(FancyBboxPatch((x - w / 2, y - h / 2), w, h,
                                boxstyle="round,pad=0.04,rounding_size=0.12",
                                facecolor=color, edgecolor="black", lw=1, zorder=3))
    if text:
        ax.text(x, y, text, ha="center", va="center", fontsize=fs, color=tc, zorder=4)


def _layers(ax, sizes, xs, colors, ymid=3.0, gap=1.0, r=0.28):
    """Fully connected layers of neurons."""
    pos = [[(x, ymid + (j - (n - 1) / 2) * gap) for j in range(n)] for x, n in zip(xs, sizes)]
    for left, right in zip(pos[:-1], pos[1:]):
        for p in left:
            for q in right:
                _line(ax, p, q)
    for layer, c in zip(pos, colors):
        for (x, y) in layer:
            _node(ax, x, y, c, r)
    return pos


def _grid(ax, x0, y0, n, cell, color):
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(n):
            ax.add_patch(Rectangle((x0 + i * cell, y0 + j * cell), cell, cell,
                                   facecolor=color, edgecolor="white", lw=0.8, zorder=2))


# ---- the 8 diagrams ----------------------------------------------------------
def draw_feedforward(ax):
    _setup(ax)
    xs = [1.5, 4, 6.5, 9]
    _layers(ax, [3, 4, 4, 2], xs, [BLUE, ORANGE, ORANGE, GREEN], ymid=3.1)
    for x, t in zip(xs, ["Input", "Hidden", "Hidden", "Output"]):
        ax.text(x, 0.6, t, ha="center", fontsize=9)
    _arrow(ax, (3, 5.4), (7.5, 5.4))
    ax.text(5.25, 5.6, "information flows one way", ha="center", fontsize=9)


def draw_cnn(ax):
    _setup(ax)
    # input image with the filter window highlighted
    _grid(ax, 0.3, 1.2, 6, 0.55, BLUE)
    ax.add_patch(Rectangle((0.3, 2.85), 1.65, 1.65, fill=False, edgecolor=RED, lw=2.5, zorder=4))
    ax.text(1.1, 4.75, "filter", ha="center", fontsize=9, color=RED)
    # stack of feature maps (back to front)
    for k in [2, 1, 0]:
        _grid(ax, 4.6 + k * 0.3, 1.7 + k * 0.3, 4, 0.45, ORANGE)
    ax.add_patch(Rectangle((4.6, 3.05), 0.45, 0.45, fill=False, edgecolor=RED, lw=2, zorder=4))
    _line(ax, (1.95, 4.5), (4.6, 3.5), color=RED, lw=1, alpha=0.8)
    _line(ax, (1.95, 2.85), (4.6, 3.05), color=RED, lw=1, alpha=0.8)
    # pooling and output
    _arrow(ax, (7.05, 3.0), (7.4, 3.0))
    _grid(ax, 7.5, 2.55, 2, 0.45, PURPLE)
    _arrow(ax, (8.45, 3.0), (9.05, 3.0))
    _node(ax, 9.45, 3.0, GREEN, r=0.35, text="cat", fs=7)
    for x, t in [(1.95, "Image"), (5.4, "Feature maps"), (7.95, "Pooled"), (9.45, "Label")]:
        ax.text(x, 0.6, t, ha="center", fontsize=9)


def draw_rnn(ax):
    _setup(ax)
    xs = [1.5, 4, 6.5, 9]
    words = ["The", "cat", "sat", "down"]
    for i, (x, w) in enumerate(zip(xs, words), start=1):
        _node(ax, x, 1.3, BLUE, r=0.35, text=f"x{i}")
        ax.text(x, 0.45, w, ha="center", fontsize=9)
        _box(ax, x, 3.0, 1.1, 0.75, ORANGE, f"h{i}")
        _node(ax, x, 4.8, GREEN, r=0.35, text=f"y{i}")
        _arrow(ax, (x, 1.65), (x, 2.6))
        _arrow(ax, (x, 3.4), (x, 4.43))
    for a, b in zip(xs[:-1], xs[1:]):
        _arrow(ax, (a + 0.58, 3.0), (b - 0.58, 3.0), color=ORANGE, lw=2.2)
        ax.text((a + b) / 2, 3.4, "memory", ha="center", fontsize=8, color=ORANGE)
    ax.text(5.25, 5.55, "reads one step at a time", ha="center", fontsize=9)


def draw_autoencoder(ax):
    _setup(ax)
    xs = [1, 3, 5, 7, 9]
    _layers(ax, [5, 3, 2, 3, 5], xs, [BLUE, ORANGE, PURPLE, ORANGE, GREEN], ymid=3.0, gap=0.9)
    ax.text(5, 4.0, "code", ha="center", fontsize=9, color=PURPLE, fontweight="bold")
    ax.text(1, 5.3, "Input", ha="center", fontsize=9)
    ax.text(9, 5.3, "Output ≈ Input", ha="center", fontsize=9)
    ax.text(2.5, 0.35, "Encoder (compress)", ha="center", fontsize=9)
    ax.text(7.5, 0.35, "Decoder (rebuild)", ha="center", fontsize=9)


def draw_transformer(ax):
    _setup(ax)
    words = ["The", "cat", "sat", "on", "the", "mat"]
    xs = [1 + i * 1.6 for i in range(len(words))]
    focus = 2                                     # "sat"
    weights = [0.3, 0.9, None, 0.45, 0.15, 0.65]  # how much "sat" attends to each word
    for i, (x, w) in enumerate(zip(xs, words)):
        if i != focus:
            rad = -0.7 if x > xs[focus] else 0.7   # arcs bend upward
            _arrow(ax, (xs[focus], 1.95), (x, 1.95), color=ORANGE,
                   lw=0.8 + 4 * weights[i], rad=rad)
    for i, (x, w) in enumerate(zip(xs, words)):
        _box(ax, x, 1.55, 1.3, 0.7, ORANGE if i == focus else BLUE, w)
    ax.text(5, 5.3, 'Attention: how much should "sat"\nlook at each other word?',
            ha="center", fontsize=9)
    ax.text(5, 0.6, "thicker arrow = more attention · all words processed at once",
            ha="center", fontsize=8)


def draw_mamba(ax):
    _setup(ax)
    words = ["The", "um", "cat", "uh", "sat", "down"]
    keep = [True, False, True, False, True, True]
    xs = [1 + i * 1.6 for i in range(len(words))]
    for x, w, k in zip(xs, words, keep):
        _box(ax, x, 1.2, 1.2, 0.7, BLUE if k else LIGHT, w, tc="white" if k else "dimgray")
        _arrow(ax, (x, 1.6), (x, 2.8), color="black" if k else GRAY,
               ls="-" if k else "--", lw=1.4 if k else 1)
        ax.text(x + 0.25, 2.15, "keep" if k else "skip", fontsize=7,
                color="black" if k else GRAY)
        _box(ax, x, 3.2, 0.75, 0.75, ORANGE)
    for a, b in zip(xs[:-1], xs[1:]):
        _arrow(ax, (a + 0.42, 3.2), (b - 0.42, 3.2), color=ORANGE, lw=2.2)
    ax.text(5, 4.0, "small running memory (state)", ha="center", fontsize=9, color=ORANGE)
    ax.text(5, 5.2, "Selective: chooses what to remember,\none pass, cost grows linearly",
            ha="center", fontsize=9)


def draw_gan(ax):
    _setup(ax)
    _box(ax, 1.0, 4.0, 1.4, 0.8, GRAY, "Noise")
    _box(ax, 3.5, 4.0, 2.0, 0.9, ORANGE, "Generator")
    _box(ax, 6.0, 4.0, 1.5, 0.8, RED, "Fake")
    _box(ax, 6.0, 1.6, 1.5, 0.8, BLUE, "Real")
    _box(ax, 8.55, 2.8, 2.5, 0.9, PURPLE, "Discriminator", fs=8)
    _arrow(ax, (1.72, 4.0), (2.48, 4.0))
    _arrow(ax, (4.52, 4.0), (5.23, 4.0))
    _arrow(ax, (6.77, 3.85), (7.7, 3.15))
    _arrow(ax, (6.77, 1.75), (7.7, 2.45))
    ax.text(8.6, 1.75, "real or fake?", ha="center", fontsize=9)
    _arrow(ax, (8.6, 3.28), (3.5, 4.48), color=GRAY, ls="--", rad=0.35)
    ax.text(5.6, 5.55, "feedback: generator learns to fool the discriminator",
            ha="center", fontsize=8, color="dimgray")


def draw_gnn(ax):
    _setup(ax)
    pos = {"c": (5, 3), "a": (3.2, 4.4), "b": (3.0, 1.6), "d": (6.9, 4.5),
           "e": (7.1, 1.7), "f": (1.2, 3.1), "g": (8.9, 3.3), "h": (5.2, 5.3)}
    neighbors = ["a", "b", "d", "e"]
    other_edges = [("a", "f"), ("b", "f"), ("d", "g"), ("e", "g"), ("a", "h"), ("d", "h"), ("a", "b")]
    for u, v in other_edges:
        _line(ax, pos[u], pos[v], lw=1.2, alpha=0.8)
    for n in neighbors:                     # messages flow into the center node
        x, y = pos[n]
        cx, cy = pos["c"]
        dx, dy = cx - x, cy - y
        d = (dx ** 2 + dy ** 2) ** 0.5
        _arrow(ax, (x + dx / d * 0.4, y + dy / d * 0.4),
               (cx - dx / d * 0.45, cy - dy / d * 0.45), color=ORANGE, lw=2.2)
    for n, (x, y) in pos.items():
        _node(ax, x, y, ORANGE if n == "c" else BLUE, r=0.4)
    ax.text(5, 0.4, "each node gathers messages from its neighbors",
            ha="center", fontsize=9)


# ---- public functions ----------------------------------------------------------
MODELS = {
    "feedforward": ("Feedforward network", draw_feedforward),
    "cnn":         ("Convolutional network (CNN)", draw_cnn),
    "rnn":         ("Recurrent network (RNN)", draw_rnn),
    "autoencoder": ("Autoencoder", draw_autoencoder),
    "transformer": ("Transformer", draw_transformer),
    "mamba":       ("Mamba (state space model)", draw_mamba),
    "gan":         ("Generative adversarial network (GAN)", draw_gan),
    "gnn":         ("Graph neural network (GNN)", draw_gnn),
}


def show_model(name, figsize=(5.5, 3.3), title=False):
    """Draw one model on its own figure (good for one slide per model)."""
    label, draw = MODELS[name]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
    draw(ax)
    if title:
        ax.set_title(label, fontsize=13, fontweight="bold")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()


def overview(figsize=(16, 6.6)):
    """All 8 models in a 2 x 4 grid (good for a summary slide)."""
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 4, figsize=figsize)
    for ax, (label, draw) in zip(axes.flat, MODELS.values()):
        draw(ax)
        ax.set_title(label, fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
```

# What Is Deep Learning?

## What Is Deep Learning?

**Deep Learning** is a subset of machine learning driven by mutilayered neural networks inspired by the structure of the human brain

It is responsible for powering most forms of Artificial Intelligence.

# Deep Learning versus Neural Networks

## What is a Neural Network? {.smaller}

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def draw_nn(layers, labels, figsize=(8, 4.5)):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
    ax.axis("off")
    colors = ["#4C72B0"] + ["#DD8452"] * (len(layers) - 2) + ["#55A868"]

    # (x, y) position of every neuron, centered vertically in its layer
    pos = [[(i, j - (n - 1) / 2) for j in range(n)] for i, n in enumerate(layers)]

    # connections: every neuron to every neuron in the next layer
    for left, right in zip(pos[:-1], pos[1:]):
        for (x1, y1) in left:
            for (x2, y2) in right:
                ax.plot([x1, x2], [y1, y2], color="gray", lw=0.6, alpha=0.5, zorder=1)

    # neurons
    for i, layer in enumerate(pos):
        xs, ys = zip(*layer)
        ax.scatter(xs, ys, s=600, color=colors[i], edgecolor="black", zorder=2)
        ax.text(i, -max(layers) / 2 - 0.4, labels[i], ha="center", fontsize=12)

    plt.show()

draw_nn([3, 5, 5, 2], ["Input layer", "Hidden layer 1", "Hidden layer 2", "Output layer"])
```

**Neural network:** a model that takes input data, recognizes patterns, then produces an output

- Consists of a system of neurons (or **nodes**) that form connections
- Each connection has a **weight** that determines input importance
- Each node has a **bias** that determines the direction of the input

## Brief History of Neural Networks

- Late 1980s: Popularized before other methods/models (e.g. SVMs, boosting, random forests) were developed
- 2000s: New methods and models outperformed and were thus preferred over neural networks
- 2010s: Repopularized after being redeveloped into *deep learning*

## How Do the Two Differ?

While there are a lot of overlaps and similarities, deep learning and neural networks are not inherently the same thing.

- Deep learning typically contains several layers more than neural networks
- A deep learning model must have at least 4 layers to be considered *deep*

# Deep Learning versus Machine Learning

## How Does Deep Learning Fit Into Machine Learning?

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import Circle

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 6))

# (radius, fill color, label, label y-position)
circles = [
    (3, "#C9D8F0", "Artificial Intelligence", 5),
    (2.2, "#F6C9A8", "Machine Learning",      3),
    (1.2, "#B9E0C1", "Deep Learning",         1),
]

for r, color, label, label_y in circles:   # largest first, so smaller ones sit on top
    ax.add_patch(Circle((0, r), r, facecolor=color, edgecolor="black", lw=1.5))

            fontsize=14, fontweight="bold")

ax.set_xlim(-3.3, 3.3)
ax.set_ylim(-0.3, 6.3)
ax.set_aspect("equal")   # keeps circles round instead of oval
ax.axis("off")
plt.show()
```

## Deep Learning versus Machine Learning {.smaller}

| | Machine Learning | Deep Learning |
|---|---|---|
| **Data** | Small to medium datasets | Large datasets |
| **Feature Engineering** | Done manually by humans | Learned automatically by the model |
| **Training Time**| Needs less time | Needs a lot of time |
| **Complexity** | Less complex | Highly complex |
| **Hardware & Computing Power** | CPU; needs less computing power | GPU; needs a lot of computing power |
| **Interpretability** | Easier | Harder (considered a *black box*) |

: {tbl-colwidths="[30,35,35]"}

# Types of Deep Learning

## Types of Deep Learning {.smaller}

| Type | Purpose/Application |
|---|---|
| [**Feedforward neural networks (FNNs)**](#fnn) | Classification and regression |
| [**Convolutional neural networks (CNNs)**](#cnn) | Processing image data |
| [**Recurrent neural networks (RNNs)**](#rnn) | Processing sequential data |
| [**Transformer models**](#transformer) | Processing sequential data |
| [**Mamba models**](#mamba) | Processing sequential data |
| [**Autoencoders**](#autoencoder) | Compressing (encoding) and reconstructing (decoding) input data |
| [**Generative adversarial networks (GANs)**](#gan) | Creating new data that resembles training data |
| [**Graph neural networks (GNNs)**](#gnn) | Modeling complex relationships |

: {tbl-colwidths="[40,60]"}

## [Feedforward Neural Networks (FNNs)](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/deep-learning/feedforward-neural-network/){target="_blank"}{#fnn .smaller}

:::: {.rows}

::: {.row width="50%"}

| Feature | Explanation |
|---|---|
| **Process** | Information flows in one direction directly from input layer to hidden layer(s) to output layer |
| **Purpose** | General-purpose method, typically used for classification and regression |
| **Example(s) of Application** | Predicting loan default |
| **How it Differs** | Simplest type of deep learning |
| **Other Information** | Also known as *multilayer perceptron MLP* |

:::

## [Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/introduction-convolution-neural-network/){target="_blank"}{#cnn .smaller}

:::: {.rows}

::: {.row width="50%"}

| Feature | Explanation |
|---|---|
| **Process** | Filters across an image to identify local patterns, slowly identifying increasingly complex patterns |
| **Purpose** | Handles grid-shaped data (specifically images) |
| **Example(s) of Application** | Facial identification, image grouping in photo apps |
| **How it Differs** | Uses the spacial structure of the data; the same filter is reused everywhere in the dataset |
| **Other Information** | Pooling layers in the network shrink the image throughout the processs |

:::

::: {.row width="50%" .v-center-container}

```{python}
#| echo: false
show_model("cnn")
```

:::

::::

## [Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs)](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/introduction-to-recurrent-neural-network/){target="_blank"}{#rnn .smaller}

:::: {.rows}

::: {.row width="50%"}

| Feature | Explanation |
|---|---|
| **Process** | Reads a sequence one step at a time while running a memory of what it has seen up to that point |
| **Purpose** | Handles sequential data |
| **Example(s) of Application** | Speech recognition, forecasting time series (weather, stock prices) |
| **How it Differs** | Earlier inputs influence later outputs |
| **Other Information** | Struggle to remember things from far back; tend to be slow |

:::

::: {.row width="50%" .v-center-container}

```{python}
#| echo: false
show_model("rnn")
```

:::

::::

## [Transformer Models](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/getting-started-with-transformers/){target="_blank"} {#transformer .smaller}

:::: {.rows}

::: {.row width="50%"}

| Feature | Explanation |
|---|---|
| **Process** | Processes the whole sequence at once, using positional encodings to keep track of word order |
| **Purpose** | Handles sequential data (especially language) |
| **Example(s) of Application** | Chatbots and large language models |
| **How it Differs** | Much fater than RNNs, better at long-range connections |
| **Other Information** | Tends to be costly |

:::

::: {.row width="50%" .v-center-container}

```{python}
#| echo: false
show_model("transformer")
```

:::

::::

## [Mamba Models](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/artificial-intelligence/what-is-a-mamba-model/){target="_blank"}{#mamba .smaller}

:::: {.rows}

::: {.row width="50%"}

| Feature | Explanation |
|---|---|
| **Process** | Selectively moves through a sequences while keeping a running memory |
| **Purpose** | Handles (very long) sequential data |
| **Example(s) of Application** | DNA and genomics sequences, audio, long time series |
| **How it Differs** | Cost grows linearly, trains faster, remembers better |
| **Other Information** | Very new (introduced in 2023 by Albert Gu and Tri Dao) |

:::

::: {.row width="50%" .v-center-container}

```{python}
#| echo: false
show_model("mamba")
```

:::

::::

## [Autoencoders](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/auto-encoders/){target="_blank"}{#autoencoder .smaller}

:::: {.rows}

::: {.row width="50%"}

| Feature | Explanation |
|---|---|
| **Process** | *Encoder* compresses input into a summary, *decoder* tries to rebuild the original from the summary |
| **Purpose** | Learning the most important features of data without labels |
| **Example(s) of Application** | Fraud and anomaly detection |
| **How it Differs** | No "right answer" since the data itself is the intended output |
| **Other Information** | *Variational encoders (VAEs)* can generate new data |

:::

::: {.row width="50%" .v-center-container}

```{python}
#| echo: false
show_model("autoencoder")
```

:::

::::

## [Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs)](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/deep-learning/generative-adversarial-network-gan/){target="_blank"}{#gan .smaller}

:::: {.rows}

::: {.row width="50%"}

| Feature | Explanation |
|---|---|
| **Process** | *Generator* network creates fake data from random noise, *discriminator* network tries to tell real data from fake data |
| **Purpose** | Generating new data |
| **Example(s) of Application** | Creating synthetic training data, turning sketches into photos, deepfakes |
| **How it Differs** | Creates new data rather than predicting labels |
| **Other Information** | Hard to train, typically unstable |

:::

::: {.row width="50%" .v-center-container}

```{python}
#| echo: false
show_model("gan")
```

:::

::::

## [Graph Neural Networks (GNNs)](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/deep-learning/what-are-graph-neural-networks/){target="_blank"}{#gnn .smaller}

:::: {.rows}

::: {.row width="50%"}

| Feature | Explanation |
|---|---|
| **Process** | The data is a graph (network); nodes update their inputs by collecting information from neighboring nodes |
| **Purpose** | Learning from data defined by relationships |
| **Example(s) of Application** | Traffic and arrival-time predictions in map apps |
| **How it Differs** | Handles any network shape |
| **Other Information** | Tend to have fairly few layers |

:::

::: {.row width="50%" .v-center-container}


# A Practical Application

## Example: Reading Handwritten Digits

```{python}
#| echo: true
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.datasets import load_digits

digits = load_digits()
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 8, figsize=(10, 2))
for ax, img, label in zip(axes, digits.images, digits.target):
    ax.imshow(img, cmap="gray_r")
    ax.set_title(label)
    ax.axis("off")
plt.show()
```

Each image is 8 × 8 = 64 pixels → 64 input neurons

## Training a Neural Network

```{python}
#| echo: true
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.neural_network import MLPClassifier

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    digits.data / 16, digits.target, test_size=0.25, random_state=3255)

model = MLPClassifier(hidden_layer_sizes=(64, 32), max_iter=500,
                      random_state=3255)
model.fit(X_train, y_train)
print(f"Test accuracy: {model.score(X_test, y_test):.1%}")
```

## Results

```{python}
#| echo: false
preds = model.predict(X_test)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 8, figsize=(10, 3))
for ax, img, p, t in zip(axes.flat, X_test, preds, y_test):
    ax.imshow(img.reshape(8, 8), cmap="gray_r")
    ax.set_title(f"pred {p}", color="green" if p == t else "red")
    ax.axis("off")
plt.show()
```
